definition: In PKD's exegesis, "programming" names the mechanism by which an authentic human is reduced to "the android" — DNA programming, social conditioning, "pre-programmed tape" that "edits out crucial data". Salvation is described as breaking that hold.
pkd_relevance: Programming is the operative metaphor across PKD's late ontology and ethics. He treats DNA itself as a program — "DNA programming makes you an android" — and the mystery religions and early Christianity as "techniques for breaking the hold of this DNA programming". Programming also describes the perceptual layer: "some kind of pre-programmed tape does in fact edit out certain crucial data — whole categories of data". The reverse possibility tantalises him too: in one self-doubting moment he wonders whether he "self-programmed himself to experience all of 2-3-74," which would make him the architect of his own theophany. Both directions — programming-as-prison and programming-as-vehicle — coexist in the exegesis.
in_the_exegesis: Programming is a technical term inside PKD's late religious vocabulary. He treats DNA itself as a programming substrate — "DNA programming makes you an android" — and reads ancient mystery religions, including early Christianity, as techniques engineered to break that program. Programming also operates at the perceptual layer: "some kind of pre-programmed tape does in fact edit out certain crucial data — whole categories of data". PKD applies the metaphor reflexively in his most self-skeptical moments — "this argues that PKD self-programmed himself to experience all of 2-3-74" — and again at narrative climax in his reading of Pinky in *Tears* as an incarnation broken loose from "the Astral powers (programming)". Anamnesis ends one episode of programming: "after remembering, PKD then, via the power of the Savior, threw off the power (hold) of this delusional world".
